segments.he: עַל יְדֵי תְּפִלָּה וְשִׂיחָה בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין קוֹנוֹ הוּא מְנַצֵּחַ בְּוַדַּאי
segments.en: For the essence of teshuvah is crying out and imploring Hashem, as it is written: "the face of Hashem is against evildoers... they cried out and Hashem heard" [Tehillim 34:17–18] — and the commentators explain this in its simple sense: that when these very evildoers cry out to Hashem, then Hashem hears and saves them from all their troubles. And similarly our Rabbis of blessed memory taught: Crying out is good for a person, both before a decree is issued and after a decree is issued. And this is explained in countless places — the very great value of crying out to Hashem always, even as one is. As is most clearly expressed in the psalm of Hodu that is recited on Friday evenings: "They wandered in the wilderness... and they cried out" [Tehillim 107:4–6]; "those who sat in darkness and the shadow of death, bound in affliction and iron... and they cried out" [ibid. 107:10–13]; "fools through the path of their transgressions... and they cried out" [ibid. 107:17–19]; "those who go down to the sea... they rise to the heavens, they plunge to the depths... and they cried out" [ibid. 107:23–28]. For this entire psalm speaks of all the descents and ascents that pass over those who wish to draw close to Hashem. And the universal counsel against all kinds of confusions and obstacles and incitements — over all of them: "they cried out to Hashem in their straits, and He saved them from their distress." For when a person cries out to Hashem about the extent of his distance from Him, he draws upon himself the holiness of Yom Kippur, which is the aspect of teshuvah — and then the sovereignty is nourished from voices and cries. Understand this well for practical purposes — even for one who does not comprehend this hint of the esoteric in the kavanos — how very beautiful is crying out for a person always, and never to despair of crying out throughout all one's days, whatever may come.

segments.he: כָּל נִצְחוֹן מַלְכוּת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבּוּר כַּנַּ"ל. וְזֶה בְּחִינַת כָּל סֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים שֶׁיָּסַד דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא שׁרֶשׁ מַלְכוּת מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁהוּא הָיָה לוֹחֵם מִלְחֲמוֹת ה' כָּל יָמָיו בְּגַשְׁמִיּוּת וְרוּחָנִיּוּת וְנִצַּח כֻּלָּם עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבּוּר פֶּה דְּהַיְנוּ עַל יְדֵי רִבּוּי תְּפִלּוֹת בְּלִי שִׁעוּר עַד שֶׁכָּלַל כֻּלָּם בְּרוּחַ קָדְשׁוֹ וְסֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים. וְעַל כֵּן זָכָה בֶּאֱמֶת לְמַלְכוּת נִצְחִי שֶׁהִיא מַלְכוּת מָשִׁיחַ. וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת לַמְנַצֵּחַ שֶׁהִתְחִיל בָּהֶם רב הַמִּזְמוֹרִים שֶׁבִּתְהִלִּים. כִּי זֶה עִקַּר עִנְיַן תְּהִלִּים שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת תְּפִלּוֹת וְשִׁירוֹת וְתִשְׁבָּחוֹת כְּלָלִיּוּת הַדִּבּוּר הַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁל זִכְרוֹן עוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁאָז נַּעֲסֹק רַק בָּזֶה לְהוֹדוֹת וּלְהַלֵּל לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ.
segments.en: Through our meriting to come to the Tzaddikim on Rosh HaShanah, they draw into us the holiness of daas, until on Yom Kippur we can effect the request of Selach na [please forgive]. For they make known to us the boundless greatness of His compassion, that He desires our crying out and our entreaty always — and they strengthen us to cry out always to Hashem, which is the aspect of Yom Kippur as above. And through this all the distant ones are drawn close to Hashem. And therefore on Rosh HaShanah we begin to engage in voices and outcries to Hashem, in the aspect of "from the depths I called to You, Hashem" [Tehillim 130:1] — though the primary beginning is through the commandment of hearing the voice of the shofar. For through the commandment of the voice of the shofar — which is a very powerful voice — through this an illumination is drawn upon Yisrael's daas so they do not despair of mercy ever, but cry out always to Hashem.

segments.he: כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה כָּל הָאוֹמֵר תְּהִלִּים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה זוֹכֶה לְאָמְרָהּ לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
segments.en: And we engage in voices and outcries throughout all the Ten Days of Repentance, until on Yom Kippur every single person in Yisrael merits the totality of the holy voices — which are five voices, corresponding to the five prayers that every person in Yisrael merits to pray on Yom Kippur. And through receiving these five voices on Yom Kippur, one merits to draw upon oneself the holiness of these voices forever — meaning to always cry out to Hashem and never despair of crying out. For through this one will certainly merit drawing close to Hashem from wherever one is. And on Sukkos it is revealed that not only have we merited to receive from the Tzaddik on Rosh HaShanah — to cry out always to Hashem — but we have also merited to receive and to teach others as well, the illumination of daas described above, so they not despair ever, only cry out always to Hashem. For Hashem is still with them, for His glory fills the entire earth — and this is the aspect of the commandment of the Four Species.

segments.he: וְעִקַּר אֲמִירַת תְּהִלִּים שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת כָּל הַדִּבּוּרִים הַקְּדוֹשִׁים שֶׁאוֹמְרִים בִּשְׁבִיל זִכְרוֹן עוֹלָם הַבָּא כַּנַּ"ל. הָעִקָּר הוּא בִּבְחִינַת לַמְנַצֵּחַ שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לְהִתְגַּבֵּר בָּזֶה בְּנִצָּחוֹן גָּדוֹל מַמָּשׁ. כְּמוֹ הַלּוֹחֵם מִלְחָמָה שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִזָּהֵר שֶׁלּא יְאַבֵּד אֶת לְבָבוֹ. וְיֵשׁ בֵּין שָׂרֵי הַמִּלְחָמָה כַּמָּה לִמּוּדִים עַל זֶה לְחַזֵּק אֶת לֵב אַנְשֵׁי הַחַיִל בִּשְׁעַת הַמִּלְחָמָה שֶׁלּא יְאַבְּדוּ לְבָבָם. כְּמוֹ כֵן מַמָּשׁ הִיא בְּעִנְיָן זֶה שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לְחַזֵּק אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּכָל עֵת מְאד וְלֵידַע וּלְהַאֲמִין שֶׁאֵיךְ שֶׁהוּא יֵשׁ כּחַ גָּדוֹל לְהַדִּבּוּר מְאד מְאד. כִּי עִקַּר הַנִּצָּחוֹן עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבּוּר כַּנַּ"ל. וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת לַמְנַצֵּחַ שֶׁהִזְכִּיר בְּכָל פַּעַם קדֶם הַמִּזְמוֹר. כְּאוֹמֵר וּמַזְכִּיר וּמַזְהִיר לְכָל מִי שֶׁרוֹצֶה לִכְנס לִלְחֹם מִלְחֶמֶת ה' שֶׁהוּא מֻכְרָח בָּזֶה. כִּי רַק בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה נִבְרָא וְהוּא מְלַמְּדָם לְכָל אֶחָד שֶׁכָּל מִי שֶׁרוֹצֶה לִהְיוֹת מְנַצֵּחַ בְּמִלְחָמָה זאת יאמַר מִזְמוֹר זֶה אוֹ מִזְמוֹר זֶה בְּפֶה מָלֵא. וְזֶהוּ לַמְנַצֵּחַ וְהָבֵן. כִּי הוּא מַמָּשׁ כְּעֵין פֵּרוּשׁ רַשִׁ"י שֶׁפֵּרֵשׁ לַמְנַצֵּחַ שֶׁהוּא בִּשְׁבִיל הַלֵּוִי שֶׁמְּנַצֵּחַ בְּשִׁיר וְכוּ'.
segments.en: This is the meaning of: "And you shall speak of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up" [Devarim 6:7]. For one must always speak of Torah and fear of Heaven, and attach oneself to the point that belongs to one's heart at that time — according to the time. Whether one is at home or on the road, whether it is day or night — for there is a time and season for every purpose under the heavens. And this is the aspect of: "for this let every devout one pray to You at a time of finding" [Tehillim 32:6] — at a time of finding specifically, to always merit finding the point according to the time and the moment.

segments.he: אַךְ אֲנַחְנוּ פֵּרַשְׁנוּ לַמְנַצֵּחַ עַל הַכּל כַּנַּ"ל. וְכֵן הוּא מְחַזֵּק אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּדִבּוּרוֹ וְאוֹמֵר עַל עַצְמוֹ לַמְנַצֵּחַ מִזְמוֹר לְדָוִד.
segments.en: For certainly no person can know all this in detail — only he must always believe, in every place he is, at every time and moment, at whatever level he is, in ascent or descent — even if the descent is, Heaven forbid, as it is. He must know and believe always that certainly there is now a holy point belonging to his heart at precisely that time, to which he must attach himself — and through this he will be rectified from wherever he is. And for this much prayer and supplication are required, in the aspect of: "for this let every devout one pray to You at a time of finding" — at a time of finding, specifically.

segments.he: שֶׁהַמִּזְמוֹר הַזֶּה הוּא לְדָוִד שֶׁהוּא הַמְנַצֵּחַ אֶת הַכּל בְּדִבּוּרוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ. כִּי כֵן צְרִיכִין לְחַזֵּק אֶת עַצְמוֹ הַרְבֵּה כְּשֶׁרוֹצִין לַעֲסֹק בִּתְפִלָּה וְשִׂיחָה וְדִבּוּר בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין קוֹנוֹ. וּלְהַאֲמִין שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי יְנַצַּח עַל יְדֵי זֶה אִם יִהְיֶה חָזָק בָּזֶה לַעֲסֹק בָּזֶה כָּל יָמָיו עַד הַסּוֹף עַד שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשׁוֹ יִהְיֶה אֵיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא מְנַצֵּחַ בְּוַדַּאי. כִּי אֵיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כְּבָר נִצַּח הַרְבֵּה עַל יְדֵי דִּבּוּרוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁדִּבֵּר וּבִקֵּשׁ מֵה' יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהִתְקָרֵב אֵלָיו. כִּי כָּל מַה שֶּׁעוֹשִׂין בִּשְׁבִיל נִצָּחוֹן דִּקְדֻשָּׁה נִשְׁאָר קַיָּם לְעוֹלָם בִּפְרָט דִּבּוּר וְקוֹל שֶׁל תְּפִלָּה שֶׁיָּקָר מֵהַכּל.
segments.en: For this is the very essence of hisbodidus and conversation between oneself and one's Maker — which Rabbainu of blessed memory urged upon us so many times. For the way of a person who wishes to engage in this is that it always seems to him that just now he cannot speak, that he does not know what to say, that his heart is very closed — as everyone who has entered into this knows. And all this is because at every moment the forces of shame — the broken-heartedness — strengthen themselves and seek to conceal and hide from him the light of his holy point that belongs to his heart at that time. Therefore it seems to him that just then he cannot speak. But in truth this is complete falsehood, and it is only the work of the adversary — for if one accepts this, it will always seem so, that just now he has no heart to speak, and he will never speak. But in truth he must strengthen himself and know and believe that there is no moment in the world when he cannot connect himself to the point belonging to his heart at that time. Therefore he must force himself greatly to speak as best he can, and to seek and search in his words for his holy point. And if he strengthens and exerts himself to force open his mouth to speak always, Hashem will certainly help him and open his mouth and his heart, until he always merits connecting to the point belonging to his heart at that time — and through this all will be repaired. And there is still much to say about this, but it is impossible to explain such matters properly in writing. One who truly desires will understand a little from these words and strengthen himself in hisbodidus and conversation between himself and his Maker, and with his companions and his teacher, always, whatever the situation.

segments.he: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזּהַר מָאן נָצַח מָאן דְּאָחֵיד מָאנָא קְרָבָא בִּידוֹהִי. וְהַדָּבָר תָּמוּהַּ בְּעֵינַי. מַה זֶּה סִימָן עַל נִצָּחוֹן מֵחֲמַת שֶׁאוֹחֵז הַכְּלִי זַיִן בְּיָדוֹ הֲלא גַּם הַחוֹלֵק וְהַלּוֹחֵם נֶגְדּוֹ אוֹחֵז גַּם כֵּן כְּלִי זַיִן. וְכִי אֲחִיזַת כְּלִי זַיִן הוּא הַנִּצָּחוֹן.
segments.en: And this is: "I will bless Hashem at all times; His praise shall be in my mouth continuously" [Tehillim 34:2]. And: "Every day I will bless You and I will praise Your name forever and ever" [Tehillim 145:2]. For at all times and every day one must bless and praise Hashem and pour out one's speech before Him. For at every time and every day, at whatever level one is, there is a holy point belonging to one's heart at precisely that time — and one must attach oneself to that point.

segments.he: הֲלא מִקְרָא מָלֵא דִּבֵּר הַכָּתוּב אַל יִתְהַלֵּל חוֹגֵר כִּמְפַתֵּחַ (מְלָכִים א' כ'): אַךְ עַל פִּי דְּבָרֵינוּ הַמְבאָרִים לְמַעְלָה מְבאָר הָעִנְיָן הֵיטֵב. כִּי כְּבָר מְבאָר שֶׁמִּי שֶׁכַּוָּנָתוֹ אֶל הָאֱמֶת וְחוֹגֵר עַצְמוֹ לְמִלְחָמָה בִּשְׁבִיל הָאֱמֶת הוּא מְנַצֵּחַ תָּמִיד. כִּי כָּל מַה שֶּׁעוֹשֶׂה אֵיזֶה עֻבְדָּא לְצרֶךְ מִלְחֶמֶת מִצְוָה הַזּאת הוּא מְנַצֵּחַ בָּזֶה מִיָּד.
segments.en: This is the meaning of: "Blessed are they who guard justice" [Tehillim 106:3] — for what one speaks between oneself and one's Maker through which the light of the point is connected to the heart, as above, this is the aspect of mishpat [justice/judgment], through which one judges oneself and finds oneself guilty and rebukes oneself to fulfill the words of the Torah. As is understood from the words of our master, teacher, and Rabbainu of blessed memory elsewhere [Likutay Moharan 59], where he calls hisbodidus and conversation between oneself and one's Maker by the name mishpat. And also because the essential thing is to attach oneself to the point belonging to one's heart at this time — and this is the aspect of mishpat, for mishpat is the central pillar, meaning it directs the judgment precisely, not veering to the right or the left, but aiming to attach oneself to the point belonging to one's heart at exactly that time — in the aspect of: "to perform the judgment of His servant and the judgment of His people Yisrael, the matter of each day in its day" [Melachim I 8:59] — the matter of each day in its day, specifically, meaning to direct the mishpat to attach oneself to the point belonging to one's heart on that day.

segments.he: מֵאַחַר שֶׁכַּוָּנָתוֹ לַשָּׁמַיִם בֶּאֱמֶת כַּנַּ"ל. (שָׁם אוֹת יד יט):
segments.en: For there the verse speaks of prayer and conversation that one conducts between oneself and one's Maker, as it is written there at the start of the verse: "And may these my words, which I have entreated before Hashem, be close to Hashem our G-d day and night, to perform the judgment of His servant... the matter of each day in its day" — meaning that all the words and supplications with which we entreat before Hashem should be in the aspect of mishpat, the matter of each day in its day — to attach oneself always to the point belonging to one's heart at that time. And this is what is written there: "to incline our hearts to Him, to walk in all His ways" [Melachim I 8:58] — for through the aspect of mishpat, the aspect of the point described above, one merits to incline one's heart to Hashem. And this is: "Blessed are they who guard justice" — one who guards and maintains the mishpat, to attach oneself always to the point belonging to one's heart at that time — this one merits through the aspect of one who performs righteousness at all times.

aligned_segments.he: עַל יְדֵי תְּפִלָּה וְשִׂיחָה בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין קוֹנוֹ הוּא מְנַצֵּחַ בְּוַדַּאי
aligned_segments.en: For the essence of teshuvah is crying out and imploring Hashem, as it is written: "the face of Hashem is against evildoers... they cried out and Hashem heard" [Tehillim 34:17–18] — and the commentators explain this in its simple sense: that when these very evildoers cry out to Hashem, then Hashem hears and saves them from all their troubles. And similarly our Rabbis of blessed memory taught: Crying out is good for a person, both before a decree is issued and after a decree is issued. And this is explained in countless places — the very great value of crying out to Hashem always, even as one is. As is most clearly expressed in the psalm of Hodu that is recited on Friday evenings: "They wandered in the wilderness... and they cried out" [Tehillim 107:4–6]; "those who sat in darkness and the shadow of death, bound in affliction and iron... and they cried out" [ibid. 107:10–13]; "fools through the path of their transgressions... and they cried out" [ibid. 107:17–19]; "those who go down to the sea... they rise to the heavens, they plunge to the depths... and they cried out" [ibid. 107:23–28]. For this entire psalm speaks of all the descents and ascents that pass over those who wish to draw close to Hashem. And the universal counsel against all kinds of confusions and obstacles and incitements — over all of them: "they cried out to Hashem in their straits, and He saved them from their distress." For when a person cries out to Hashem about the extent of his distance from Him, he draws upon himself the holiness of Yom Kippur, which is the aspect of teshuvah — and then the sovereignty is nourished from voices and cries. Understand this well for practical purposes — even for one who does not comprehend this hint of the esoteric in the kavanos — how very beautiful is crying out for a person always, and never to despair of crying out throughout all one's days, whatever may come.

aligned_segments.he: כָּל נִצְחוֹן מַלְכוּת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבּוּר כַּנַּ"ל.
aligned_segments.en: Through our meriting to come to the Tzaddikim on Rosh HaShanah, they draw into us the holiness of daas, until on Yom Kippur we can effect the request of Selach na [please forgive].

aligned_segments.he: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת כָּל סֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים שֶׁיָּסַד דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא שׁרֶשׁ מַלְכוּת מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁהוּא הָיָה לוֹחֵם מִלְחֲמוֹת ה' כָּל יָמָיו בְּגַשְׁמִיּוּת וְרוּחָנִיּוּת וְנִצַּח כֻּלָּם עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבּוּר פֶּה דְּהַיְנוּ עַל יְדֵי רִבּוּי תְּפִלּוֹת בְּלִי שִׁעוּר עַד שֶׁכָּלַל כֻּלָּם בְּרוּחַ קָדְשׁוֹ וְסֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים.
aligned_segments.en: For they make known to us the boundless greatness of His compassion, that He desires our crying out and our entreaty always — and they strengthen us to cry out always to Hashem, which is the aspect of Yom Kippur as above.

aligned_segments.he: וְעַל כֵּן זָכָה בֶּאֱמֶת לְמַלְכוּת נִצְחִי שֶׁהִיא מַלְכוּת מָשִׁיחַ.
aligned_segments.en: And through this all the distant ones are drawn close to Hashem.

aligned_segments.he: וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת לַמְנַצֵּחַ שֶׁהִתְחִיל בָּהֶם רב הַמִּזְמוֹרִים שֶׁבִּתְהִלִּים.
aligned_segments.en: And therefore on Rosh HaShanah we begin to engage in voices and outcries to Hashem, in the aspect of "from the depths I called to You, Hashem" [Tehillim 130:1] — though the primary beginning is through the commandment of hearing the voice of the shofar.

aligned_segments.he: כִּי זֶה עִקַּר עִנְיַן תְּהִלִּים שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת תְּפִלּוֹת וְשִׁירוֹת וְתִשְׁבָּחוֹת כְּלָלִיּוּת הַדִּבּוּר הַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁל זִכְרוֹן עוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁאָז נַּעֲסֹק רַק בָּזֶה לְהוֹדוֹת וּלְהַלֵּל לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ.
aligned_segments.en: For through the commandment of the voice of the shofar — which is a very powerful voice — through this an illumination is drawn upon Yisrael's daas so they do not despair of mercy ever, but cry out always to Hashem.

aligned_segments.he: כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה כָּל הָאוֹמֵר תְּהִלִּים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה זוֹכֶה לְאָמְרָהּ לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
aligned_segments.en: And we engage in voices and outcries throughout all the Ten Days of Repentance, until on Yom Kippur every single person in Yisrael merits the totality of the holy voices — which are five voices, corresponding to the five prayers that every person in Yisrael merits to pray on Yom Kippur. And through receiving these five voices on Yom Kippur, one merits to draw upon oneself the holiness of these voices forever — meaning to always cry out to Hashem and never despair of crying out. For through this one will certainly merit drawing close to Hashem from wherever one is. And on Sukkos it is revealed that not only have we merited to receive from the Tzaddik on Rosh HaShanah — to cry out always to Hashem — but we have also merited to receive and to teach others as well, the illumination of daas described above, so they not despair ever, only cry out always to Hashem. For Hashem is still with them, for His glory fills the entire earth — and this is the aspect of the commandment of the Four Species.

aligned_segments.he: וְעִקַּר אֲמִירַת תְּהִלִּים שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת כָּל הַדִּבּוּרִים הַקְּדוֹשִׁים שֶׁאוֹמְרִים בִּשְׁבִיל זִכְרוֹן עוֹלָם הַבָּא כַּנַּ"ל. הָעִקָּר הוּא בִּבְחִינַת לַמְנַצֵּחַ שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לְהִתְגַּבֵּר בָּזֶה בְּנִצָּחוֹן גָּדוֹל מַמָּשׁ.
aligned_segments.en: This is the meaning of: "And you shall speak of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up" [Devarim 6:7].

aligned_segments.he: כְּמוֹ הַלּוֹחֵם מִלְחָמָה שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִזָּהֵר שֶׁלּא יְאַבֵּד אֶת לְבָבוֹ. וְיֵשׁ בֵּין שָׂרֵי הַמִּלְחָמָה כַּמָּה לִמּוּדִים עַל זֶה לְחַזֵּק אֶת לֵב אַנְשֵׁי הַחַיִל בִּשְׁעַת הַמִּלְחָמָה שֶׁלּא יְאַבְּדוּ לְבָבָם. כְּמוֹ כֵן מַמָּשׁ הִיא בְּעִנְיָן זֶה שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לְחַזֵּק אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּכָל עֵת מְאד וְלֵידַע וּלְהַאֲמִין שֶׁאֵיךְ שֶׁהוּא יֵשׁ כּחַ גָּדוֹל לְהַדִּבּוּר מְאד מְאד.
aligned_segments.en: For one must always speak of Torah and fear of Heaven, and attach oneself to the point that belongs to one's heart at that time — according to the time.

aligned_segments.he: כִּי עִקַּר הַנִּצָּחוֹן עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבּוּר כַּנַּ"ל. וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת לַמְנַצֵּחַ שֶׁהִזְכִּיר בְּכָל פַּעַם קדֶם הַמִּזְמוֹר. כְּאוֹמֵר וּמַזְכִּיר וּמַזְהִיר לְכָל מִי שֶׁרוֹצֶה לִכְנס לִלְחֹם מִלְחֶמֶת ה' שֶׁהוּא מֻכְרָח בָּזֶה.
aligned_segments.en: Whether one is at home or on the road, whether it is day or night — for there is a time and season for every purpose under the heavens.

aligned_segments.he: כִּי רַק בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה נִבְרָא וְהוּא מְלַמְּדָם לְכָל אֶחָד שֶׁכָּל מִי שֶׁרוֹצֶה לִהְיוֹת מְנַצֵּחַ בְּמִלְחָמָה זאת יאמַר מִזְמוֹר זֶה אוֹ מִזְמוֹר זֶה בְּפֶה מָלֵא. וְזֶהוּ לַמְנַצֵּחַ וְהָבֵן. כִּי הוּא מַמָּשׁ כְּעֵין פֵּרוּשׁ רַשִׁ"י שֶׁפֵּרֵשׁ לַמְנַצֵּחַ שֶׁהוּא בִּשְׁבִיל הַלֵּוִי שֶׁמְּנַצֵּחַ בְּשִׁיר וְכוּ'.
aligned_segments.en: And this is the aspect of: "for this let every devout one pray to You at a time of finding" [Tehillim 32:6] — at a time of finding specifically, to always merit finding the point according to the time and the moment.

aligned_segments.he: אַךְ אֲנַחְנוּ פֵּרַשְׁנוּ לַמְנַצֵּחַ עַל הַכּל כַּנַּ"ל.
aligned_segments.en: For certainly no person can know all this in detail — only he must always believe, in every place he is, at every time and moment, at whatever level he is, in ascent or descent — even if the descent is, Heaven forbid, as it is.

aligned_segments.he: וְכֵן הוּא מְחַזֵּק אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּדִבּוּרוֹ וְאוֹמֵר עַל עַצְמוֹ לַמְנַצֵּחַ מִזְמוֹר לְדָוִד.
aligned_segments.en: He must know and believe always that certainly there is now a holy point belonging to his heart at precisely that time, to which he must attach himself — and through this he will be rectified from wherever he is. And for this much prayer and supplication are required, in the aspect of: "for this let every devout one pray to You at a time of finding" — at a time of finding, specifically.

aligned_segments.he: שֶׁהַמִּזְמוֹר הַזֶּה הוּא לְדָוִד שֶׁהוּא הַמְנַצֵּחַ אֶת הַכּל בְּדִבּוּרוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ.
aligned_segments.en: For this is the very essence of hisbodidus and conversation between oneself and one's Maker — which Rabbainu of blessed memory urged upon us so many times. For the way of a person who wishes to engage in this is that it always seems to him that just now he cannot speak, that he does not know what to say, that his heart is very closed — as everyone who has entered into this knows.

aligned_segments.he: כִּי כֵן צְרִיכִין לְחַזֵּק אֶת עַצְמוֹ הַרְבֵּה כְּשֶׁרוֹצִין לַעֲסֹק בִּתְפִלָּה וְשִׂיחָה וְדִבּוּר בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין קוֹנוֹ.
aligned_segments.en: And all this is because at every moment the forces of shame — the broken-heartedness — strengthen themselves and seek to conceal and hide from him the light of his holy point that belongs to his heart at that time. Therefore it seems to him that just then he cannot speak.

aligned_segments.he: וּלְהַאֲמִין שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי יְנַצַּח עַל יְדֵי זֶה אִם יִהְיֶה חָזָק בָּזֶה לַעֲסֹק בָּזֶה כָּל יָמָיו עַד הַסּוֹף עַד שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשׁוֹ יִהְיֶה אֵיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא מְנַצֵּחַ בְּוַדַּאי.
aligned_segments.en: But in truth this is complete falsehood, and it is only the work of the adversary — for if one accepts this, it will always seem so, that just now he has no heart to speak, and he will never speak. But in truth he must strengthen himself and know and believe that there is no moment in the world when he cannot connect himself to the point belonging to his heart at that time.

aligned_segments.he: כִּי אֵיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כְּבָר נִצַּח הַרְבֵּה עַל יְדֵי דִּבּוּרוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁדִּבֵּר וּבִקֵּשׁ מֵה' יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהִתְקָרֵב אֵלָיו.
aligned_segments.en: Therefore he must force himself greatly to speak as best he can, and to seek and search in his words for his holy point. And if he strengthens and exerts himself to force open his mouth to speak always, Hashem will certainly help him and open his mouth and his heart, until he always merits connecting to the point belonging to his heart at that time — and through this all will be repaired.

aligned_segments.he: כִּי כָּל מַה שֶּׁעוֹשִׂין בִּשְׁבִיל נִצָּחוֹן דִּקְדֻשָּׁה נִשְׁאָר קַיָּם לְעוֹלָם בִּפְרָט דִּבּוּר וְקוֹל שֶׁל תְּפִלָּה שֶׁיָּקָר מֵהַכּל.
aligned_segments.en: And there is still much to say about this, but it is impossible to explain such matters properly in writing. One who truly desires will understand a little from these words and strengthen himself in hisbodidus and conversation between himself and his Maker, and with his companions and his teacher, always, whatever the situation.

aligned_segments.he: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזּהַר מָאן נָצַח מָאן דְּאָחֵיד מָאנָא קְרָבָא בִּידוֹהִי.
aligned_segments.en: And this is: "I will bless Hashem at all times; His praise shall be in my mouth continuously" [Tehillim 34:2].

aligned_segments.he: וְהַדָּבָר תָּמוּהַּ בְּעֵינַי.
aligned_segments.en: And: "Every day I will bless You and I will praise Your name forever and ever" [Tehillim 145:2].

aligned_segments.he: מַה זֶּה סִימָן עַל נִצָּחוֹן מֵחֲמַת שֶׁאוֹחֵז הַכְּלִי זַיִן בְּיָדוֹ הֲלא גַּם הַחוֹלֵק וְהַלּוֹחֵם נֶגְדּוֹ אוֹחֵז גַּם כֵּן כְּלִי זַיִן.
aligned_segments.en: For at all times and every day one must bless and praise Hashem and pour out one's speech before Him.

aligned_segments.he: וְכִי אֲחִיזַת כְּלִי זַיִן הוּא הַנִּצָּחוֹן.
aligned_segments.en: For at every time and every day, at whatever level one is, there is a holy point belonging to one's heart at precisely that time — and one must attach oneself to that point.

aligned_segments.he: הֲלא מִקְרָא מָלֵא דִּבֵּר הַכָּתוּב אַל יִתְהַלֵּל חוֹגֵר כִּמְפַתֵּחַ (מְלָכִים א' כ'):
aligned_segments.en: This is the meaning of: "Blessed are they who guard justice" [Tehillim 106:3] — for what one speaks between oneself and one's Maker through which the light of the point is connected to the heart, as above, this is the aspect of mishpat [justice/judgment], through which one judges oneself and finds oneself guilty and rebukes oneself to fulfill the words of the Torah.

aligned_segments.he: אַךְ עַל פִּי דְּבָרֵינוּ הַמְבאָרִים לְמַעְלָה מְבאָר הָעִנְיָן הֵיטֵב.
aligned_segments.en: As is understood from the words of our master, teacher, and Rabbainu of blessed memory elsewhere [Likutay Moharan 59], where he calls hisbodidus and conversation between oneself and one's Maker by the name mishpat.

aligned_segments.he: כִּי כְּבָר מְבאָר שֶׁמִּי שֶׁכַּוָּנָתוֹ אֶל הָאֱמֶת וְחוֹגֵר עַצְמוֹ לְמִלְחָמָה בִּשְׁבִיל הָאֱמֶת הוּא מְנַצֵּחַ תָּמִיד. כִּי כָּל מַה שֶּׁעוֹשֶׂה אֵיזֶה עֻבְדָּא לְצרֶךְ מִלְחֶמֶת מִצְוָה הַזּאת הוּא מְנַצֵּחַ בָּזֶה מִיָּד.
aligned_segments.en: And also because the essential thing is to attach oneself to the point belonging to one's heart at this time — and this is the aspect of mishpat, for mishpat is the central pillar, meaning it directs the judgment precisely, not veering to the right or the left, but aiming to attach oneself to the point belonging to one's heart at exactly that time — in the aspect of: "to perform the judgment of His servant and the judgment of His people Yisrael, the matter of each day in its day" [Melachim I 8:59] — the matter of each day in its day, specifically, meaning to direct the mishpat to attach oneself to the point belonging to one's heart on that day.

aligned_segments.he: מֵאַחַר שֶׁכַּוָּנָתוֹ לַשָּׁמַיִם בֶּאֱמֶת כַּנַּ"ל. (שָׁם אוֹת יד יט):
aligned_segments.en: For there the verse speaks of prayer and conversation that one conducts between oneself and one's Maker, as it is written there at the start of the verse: "And may these my words, which I have entreated before Hashem, be close to Hashem our G-d day and night, to perform the judgment of His servant... the matter of each day in its day" — meaning that all the words and supplications with which we entreat before Hashem should be in the aspect of mishpat, the matter of each day in its day — to attach oneself always to the point belonging to one's heart at that time. And this is what is written there: "to incline our hearts to Him, to walk in all His ways" [Melachim I 8:58] — for through the aspect of mishpat, the aspect of the point described above, one merits to incline one's heart to Hashem. And this is: "Blessed are they who guard justice" — one who guards and maintains the mishpat, to attach oneself always to the point belonging to one's heart at that time — this one merits through the aspect of one who performs righteousness at all times.
